newsitem.title: USA: Polar Air adds Latam country, consolidates routes.
newsitem.headline: Polar Air adds Latam country, consolidates routes.

text.p: Polar Air Cargo plans to add another Latin American country to its list of destinations, following its recent approval to consolidate all of its Latin American flights, a top company executive said Wednesday.

The U.S. Department of Transportation approved Polar's application to consolidate all its Latin American routes, Kevin Montgomery, Polar's vice- president of government and industry affairs, told Reuters.

Permitting the airline to make interim stops in Latin America where it already has the authority, "allows us to increase frequencies in each market," Montgomery said, adding that it also helps insure full loads in both directions.
Polar's new Latin American route structure will begin after January 1, he said. Montgomery declined to name the Latin American country Polar plans to serve next.
The privately held, all-cargo airline currently operates 14 Boeing 747 freighters and plans to add two to three a year for the next few years, Montgomery said.
About 50 percent of Polar's business is in Asia and the South Pacific and the rest divided between Europe and Latin America, Montgomery said.

Besides its plans in Latin America, earlier this month the DOT also awarded Polar authority to fly to Japan six flights per week. This is the first scheduled Japan service for Polar, which has flown charters in the past.
Polar will begin the Japan service "as soon as we receive authorization from Japan," said Montgomery, which will be at least 90 days from the December 6 approval by the DOT.
In the first quarter, Polar also expects to begin a service to India. "Everything is in place in the U.S, it is pending approval in India," said Montgomery.
The heavier traffic is primarily ex-India, said Montgomery, and merchandise is primarily textiles and clothing.

Polar is one of a handful of carriers that offers service from Asia to Latin America. It uses both Miami International Airport and Los Angeles International Airport as hubs for this activity. "That is predicted to be a growth sector," said Montgomery.
